digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III/VI; Maundu & Tengnäs 2005 give the same Digo name Ganga for the related Euphorbia candelabrum
other_mijikenda: Duruma: Ganga (shared, Pakia); Giriama: Kithongothongo (E. candelabrum)

teaser.en: Its name comes from *uganga*, healing, yet its white sap is so poisonous that a drop in the eye is dangerous.
teaser.sw: Jina lake linatokana na *uganga*, yaani tiba, lakini utomvu wake mweupe una sumu kali kiasi kwamba tone moja jichoni ni hatari.

summary.en: *Ganga* is a succulent tree shaped like a candelabra, with ribbed, spiny green branches full of poisonous white latex. It grows in dry bushland and on rocky hills, and is used in healing and for building.
summary.sw: *Ganga* ni mti wenye unyama wenye umbo la kinara cha mishumaa, wenye matawi ya kijani yenye mifuo na miiba yaliyojaa utomvu mweupe wenye sumu. Huota katika vichaka vikavu na kwenye vilima vya miamba, na hutumika katika tiba na ujenzi.

about.en:
*Ganga* looks more like a giant cactus than a tree. A short trunk divides into many upright, ribbed green branches, curving up like the arms of a candelabra. The ribs are lined with paired spines, and the branches do the work of leaves.

Cut or break any part of it and a thick, white latex pours out. The latex is poisonous and dangerous to the eyes.
about.sw:
*Ganga* inafanana zaidi na mpungate mkubwa kuliko mti. Shina fupi hugawanyika kuwa matawi mengi ya kijani yaliyosimama wima na yenye mifuo, yakipinda juu kama mikono ya kinara cha mishumaa. Mifuo imepangwa miiba ya jozi, na matawi hufanya kazi ya majani.

Ukikata au kuvunja sehemu yoyote yake, utomvu mzito mweupe hutiririka. Utomvu huo una sumu na ni hatari kwa macho.

where.en: It grows in dry bushland and on rocky hills, standing out against the sky with its many upright arms.
where.sw: Huota katika vichaka vikavu na kwenye vilima vya miamba, ikionekana wazi dhidi ya anga kwa mikono yake mingi iliyosimama wima.

uses.en:
Pakia records that *ganga* is used in healing various ailments.

Its wood is used for roofing, doors and beehives. The latex is dangerous to the eyes, so people handle the plant with care.
uses.sw:
Pakia anarekodi kwamba *ganga* hutumika kutibu maradhi mbalimbali.

Mbao zake hutumika kwa paa, milango na mizinga ya nyuki. Utomvu wake ni hatari kwa macho, hivyo watu huushughulikia mmea huu kwa uangalifu.

culture.en: Pakia explains that the name *ganga* comes from *uganga*, healing, reflecting the plant's place in traditional medicine.
culture.sw: Pakia anaeleza kwamba jina *ganga* linatokana na *uganga*, yaani tiba, likionyesha nafasi ya mmea huu katika tiba za jadi.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name *ganga*, which Duruma speakers share. Maundu and Tengnäs give the same Digo name for the related *Euphorbia candelabrum*, known in Giriama as *kithongothongo*. No Swahili or common English name has been recorded for this species; its scientific name is *Euphorbia nyikae*.
names.sw: Pakia anarekodi jina la Kidigo *ganga*, ambalo wazungumzaji wa Kiduruma pia hulitumia. Maundu na Tengnäs wanatoa jina hilohilo la Kidigo kwa ndugu yake *Euphorbia candelabrum*, unaojulikana kwa Kigiriama kama *kithongothongo*. Hakuna jina la Kiswahili wala jina la kawaida la Kiingereza lililorekodiwa kwa spishi hii; jina lake la kisayansi ni *Euphorbia nyikae*.

definition.en: A burning, itching latex that harms the skin and eyes, so people avoid it.
definition.sw: Utomvu unaochoma na kuwasha unaodhuru ngozi na macho, hivyo watu huuepuka.

use.en: Some people use it as a fish poison.
use.sw: Baadhi ya watu huutumia kama sumu ya kuvulia samaki.
